policy.primary: A historical text, edition, translation, or direct textual witness.
policy.secondary: Modern scholarship or a reference overview used for orientation.
policy.formal: A source for the mathematical or logical machinery rather than for a historical interpretation.
policy.unverified: The work or topic is named, but a passage-level edition has not been registered.

sources.citation: Anders Schlichtkrull and Jørgen Villadsen, Paraconsistency, Archive of Formal Proofs (2016), first released 7 December 2016
sources.note: Session Paraconsistency formalizes a countably infinite-valued paraconsistent propositional logic, with validity results, counterexamples and metatheory. It is not FDE. The release year is 2016, distinct from later development-PDF update dates. The official development entry was also consulted at https://devel.isa-afp.org/entries/Paraconsistency.html; the canonical citation is the release entry.

sources.citation: Alexander Steen and Christoph Benzmüller, Sweet SIXTEEN: Automation via Embedding into Classical Higher-Order Logic, Logic and Logical Philosophy 25(4) (2016), 535-554, DOI 10.12775/LLP.2016.021
sources.note: A higher-order embedding of the sixteen-valued generalization of Dunn-Belnap logic, with an Isabelle/HOL implementation and automated reasoning experiments. Cited as embedding and automation, not as evidence of a kernel-checked adequacy theorem or of a mechanization of the exact FDE containment theorem. Publisher record: https://apcz.umk.pl/LLP/article/view/LLP.2016.021 .

sources.citation: Dominique Larchey-Wendling, Constructive Decision via Redundancy-Free Proof-Search, Journal of Automated Reasoning 64 (2020), 1197-1219, DOI 10.1007/s10817-020-09555-y
sources.note: The publisher abstract reports an axiom-free Coq mechanization of a constructive decidability method, instantiated for implicational relevance logic. This supports a precedent for proof-assistant work on nonclassical reasoning, not a claim about FDE or the corpus's exact variable-sharing and containment results.

sources.citation: Christoph Benzmüller and Bruno Woltzenlogel Paleo, The Inconsistency in Gödel's Ontological Argument: A Success Story for AI in Metaphysics, Proceedings of the Twenty-Fifth International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI-16) (2016), 936-942
sources.note: Sections 3.2, 4.1-4.3 and 5 consulted. Section 4.3, pp. 940-941 and Figure 6, identifies the definitions and axioms used in the verified refutation and maps them to Gödel's manuscript. A methodological precedent for premise auditing and source correspondence, not a claim that the present corpus discovers a comparable historical inconsistency. Publisher bibliographic record: https://www.ijcai.org/Abstract/16/137 . No DOI was confirmed on the primary publication pages.

sources.citation: David Fuenmayor and Christoph Benzmüller, A Computational-Hermeneutic Approach for Conceptual Explicitation, in Ángel Nepomuceno-Fernández, Lorenzo Magnani, Francisco J. Salguero-Lamillar, Cristina Barés-Gómez and Matthieu Fontaine (eds.), Model-Based Reasoning in Science and Technology, Studies in Applied Philosophy, Epistemology and Rational Ethics 49 (Springer, Cham, 2019), 441-469, DOI 10.1007/978-3-030-32722-4_25
sources.note: Author preprint sections 2.1, 3.2-3.5 and 4.1-4.2 consulted; printed preprint pp. 20-23 show iterative analysis of Lowe's argument, a Nitpick countermodel, and the separation of premises from meaning postulates. These are preprint pinpoint pages, not published chapter page numbers. Publisher metadata: https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-32722-4_25 . A precedent for making interpretive choices explicit; the present corpus does not implement the full charity-guided search for adequate argument formalizations or an automated hermeneutic engine. Not to be confused with the distinct 2019 chapter Computational Hermeneutics: An Integrated Approach for the Logical Analysis of Natural-Language Arguments.

sources.citation: Christoph Benzmüller, Xavier Parent and Leendert van der Torre, Designing Normative Theories for Ethical and Legal Reasoning: LogiKEy Framework, Methodology, and Tool Support, Artificial Intelligence 287 (2020), 103348, DOI 10.1016/j.artint.2020.103348
sources.note: Author preprint v6 sections 5.1 and 7.1-7.4 consulted, especially printed preprint pp. 31-36: logic/domain/application layers, theorem-prover and model-finder checks, embedding faithfulness, and remaining interpretive open texture. These are preprint pinpoint pages. Publication DOI and journal record are independently listed by the author-maintained project: https://logikey.org/ . A methodological antecedent of layered formalization and inspectable proof/countermodel feedback; the present corpus is not an implementation of LogiKEy or an operational normative-governance system.

sources.citation: Richard P. Hayes, Dignāga on the Interpretation of Signs, Studies of Classical India 9 (Kluwer Academic Publishers, Dordrecht, 1988), DOI 10.1007/978-94-009-2899-2
sources.note: Original-book OCR consulted at pp. 122-125 on the three marks, false conclusions, and transfer between domains, and p. 127 on the subject-only asādhāraṇa case. Publication locator: https://doi.org/10.1007/978-94-009-2899-2 . These passages are historical antecedents of the scope problem, not assertions of novelty for the corpus's finite countermodel or its added bridge premise; the hosted OCR is not a new critical edition.

sources.citation: Graham Priest, Jaina Logic: A Contemporary Perspective, History and Philosophy of Logic 29(3) (2008), 263-278, DOI 10.1080/01445340701690233
sources.note: Section 3, pp. 265-266, distinguishes cumulative overlapping conditions from exact values and obtains the seven nonempty subsets of three basic values. Section 5, pp. 268-269, responds to Ganeri. The corpus's cumulative support profile and exact-support presentation must remain distinct; the seven-combination mathematics is not a novel contribution.

sources.note: The publisher's Recommended Citation explicitly gives DOI 10.55917/2151-6014.1919. Direct HTTP HEAD checks on 2026-09-20 at approximately 09:35 JST returned 302 from that DOI to the publisher article and 404 for the proposed alternative 10.31979/2151-6014(2026).170205. No alias or migration relationship was established; retain the publisher-displayed DOI. The publisher PDF was not retrieved in this check, so no claim is made about an identifier printed inside it.

sources.citation: Thomas Macaulay Ferguson, Faulty Belnap Computers and Subsystems of FDE, Journal of Logic and Computation 26(5) (2016), 1617-1636; online first 2014
sources.note: Definition 2 has FDE plus an undesignated infectious value. Theorem 3 is exactly single-premise FDE consequence plus conclusion-to-premise atom containment. Corollary 4 identifies the starred S_fde system; do not confuse it with Deutsch's unstarred system. Author version: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/274151007_Faulty_Belnap_computers_and_subsystems_of_FDE . Final-version point page not asserted.

sources.citation: Roberto Ciuni, Damian Szmuc and Thomas Macaulay Ferguson, Relevant Logics Obeying Component Homogeneity, Australasian Journal of Logic 15(2) (2018), 301-361
sources.note: Section 2.3 p. 313 directly records FDE variable sharing as familiar; Definition 11 pp. 318-319 gives the five-valued starred matrix; Corollary 11(1) p. 334 matches the single-premise atom-containment theorem. DOI 10.26686/ajl.v15i2.4864. Deutsch's original article was not consulted; the unstarred/starred distinction is taken from this paper.

sources.note: Pages 252-255 discuss school-sensitive subject exclusion and revisit On Sapaksa (1990); p. 258 explicitly identifies failure of formal entailment from the off-subject generalization. The 1990 paper was bibliographically checked, not independently read.

sources.citation: Bimal Krishna Matilal, The Central Philosophy of Jainism (Anekanta-vada), L. D. Series 79, Ahmedabad: L. D. Institute of Indology (1981)

sources.translation_policy: Used to map modern audit labels to named criteria and passage numbers; the Boolean profile relation and relevant-alternatives semantics remain project-authored paraphrases.

sources.citation: Wŏnhyo, Ten Approaches to the Harmonization of Doctrinal Disputes (Simmun hwajaeng non 十門和諍論), trans. A. Charles Muller, web edition updated 20 September 2016, introduction and §§2.1–2.4
sources.note: Muller states that only fragments of the beginning survive, with gaps, and that the translation is reconstructed from the partial preface inscription and five Haeinsa printing blocks (HBJ/HPC 1.838–841). The extant text treats existence and emptiness and the buddha-nature dispute, but supplies no sheaf-style coverage or gluing operation.
sources.translation_policy: Transliterated terms and titles follow Muller; the Lean contexts and gluing predicates are project-authored analogies and do not translate the fragmentary text.

sources.citation: A. Charles Muller, “Wŏnhyo’s Approach to Harmonization of the Mahayana Doctrines (Hwajaeng),” Acta Koreana 18.1 (2015), 9–44, especially pp. 10–13, 22–29, and 34
sources.note: Muller characterizes hwajaeng as inquiry into divergent positions’ assumptions, aims, backgrounds, and precise points of divergence; he records Simmun hwajaeng non as fragmentary at HPC 1.838–841. The study does not support overlap agreement, coverage, or gluing as Wŏnhyo’s own formal method.
sources.translation_policy: Used for bounded conceptual orientation only; the Lean interface is not presented as a translation or historical proof theory.

sources.citation: Jaimini, Mīmāṃsāsūtra 3.3.14, TextGrid/GRETIL electronic text based on B. D. Basu, Sacred Books of the Hindus 27 (Allahabad, 1923–1925)
sources.note: The Sanskrit sūtra enumerates six grounds—śruti, liṅga, vākya, prakaraṇa, sthāna, and samākhyā—and states their relative weakening because later grounds are more remote from meaning. TextGrid records the TEI version dated 2020-07-31 and revision dated 2025-05-08.
sources.translation_policy: The module paraphrases the six labels and relative ordering. Its numeric ranks, tie handling, resolver, and examples are modern formal machinery; no translation of Śabara or surrounding examples is reproduced.

sources.citation: Mingjun Tang, “Materials for the Study of Xuanzang’s Inference of Consciousness-only (wei shi bi liang 唯識比量),” Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde Südasiens 56–57 (2015–2018), 143–198
sources.note: Especially pp. 143–150 and edited materials Texts 1.1, 1.9, and 5.2. Tang documents the three qualifications, the Wŏnhyo counter-inference, and unresolved authenticity and interpretation questions.
sources.translation_policy: The module paraphrases argumentative roles and qualification scopes; it does not reproduce Tang’s translations or present one disputed historical verdict as settled.
